It is for traders who want to see the market while they trade. You connect an external wallet and sign a login challenge. The Terminal does not take custody of that wallet.

pages.title: Cross-chain swap routing, scored across providers
pages.metaDescription: Suwappu races about 10 route adapters in parallel and scores each on output, cost, speed and reliability. Default slippage 0.5%. Honeypot swaps are blocked.
pages.headline: Quote many routes. Swap on the best-scoring one.
pages.lead: One command races roughly ten route adapters in parallel, scores them, and shows you the winner. Same-chain or cross-chain. Fees 1.0% on Free, down to 0.1%.
whatItIs: Swapping across chains usually means choosing a bridge, then a DEX, then hoping the numbers hold. Suwappu asks about ten adapters at once, including CoW, Socket, Jupiter, Jito, LI.FI, CCTP, Across, Wormhole, LayerZero and Tempo DEX, and ranks the results.
The ranking is a score, not just the highest output. It weighs cost, speed and provider reliability too. You see the route and the minimum you will receive before you confirm.

pages.name: Agent API
pages.title: Agent API: quote, simulate and execute swaps over REST
pages.metaDescription: A REST API for agent swaps: quote, dry-run, then sign yourself or execute from a managed wallet. Idempotent execution, signed webhooks, 60-second quotes.
pages.headline: Quote, simulate, then execute. One REST API.
pages.lead: The Agent API is Suwappu's REST surface for cross-chain swaps. Quote and dry-run cost 1 credit each, execution costs 5, and nothing moves until you choose to execute.
whatItIs: The Agent API lives under https://api.suwappu.bot/v1/agent. You register an agent with one POST, receive a suwappu_sk_ key, and call quote, simulate and swap routes with that key in an Authorization: Bearer header.

You choose who signs. POST /swap returns an unsigned transaction for you to sign with your own wallet. POST /swap/execute signs from a managed wallet and broadcasts. Both start from the same quote, so you can dry-run first and compare the result before anything is sent.

howItWorks.title: Register
howItWorks.detail: POST /v1/agent/register with a name. The response holds your suwappu_sk_ key once; only a hash is kept. Registration is limited to 5 requests per minute per IP.

howItWorks.title: Quote
howItWorks.detail: POST /v1/agent/quote with from_token, to_token, amount, chain (or from_chain and to_chain) and your wallet_address. You get a quote_id, expected_amount_out and minimum_amount_out.

howItWorks.title: Simulate
howItWorks.detail: POST /v1/agent/swap/simulate with the quote_id and the same wallet. It reports balance, allowance, gas and revert checks without signing or broadcasting.

howItWorks.title: Swap or execute
howItWorks.detail: POST /swap returns an unsigned transaction. POST /swap/execute runs it from the managed wallet. Send an Idempotency-Key header on execute.

howItWorks.title: Track
howItWorks.detail: Poll GET /swap/status/:swapId, list with GET /swaps, or set a callback_url and receive signed webhooks.

capabilities.title: Wallet-bound quotes
capabilities.detail: A quote is valid for 60 seconds and tied to the wallet that requested it. A different wallet or agent is rejected at swap time. A quote without wallet_address cannot become a transaction.

capabilities.title: Dry run before signing
capabilities.detail: POST /swap/simulate accepts a quote_id or raw from_token, to_token and amount. Solana simulations run through Jupiter. It costs 1 credit and creates no swap record.

capabilities.title: Two signing paths
capabilities.detail: Unsigned transaction from /swap, or managed execution from /swap/execute. Pick per call, not per account.

capabilities.title: Idempotent execution
capabilities.detail: Idempotency-Key is 1 to 64 characters from A-Z a-z 0-9 _ . : -. The key is stored per agent with a request fingerprint. An invalid key returns 400 VALIDATION_ERROR.

capabilities.title: Approval-aware swaps
capabilities.detail: If a policy requires approval, /swap answers HTTP 202 with status pending, an approval_id and expires_at, instead of a transaction.

capabilities.title: Signed webhooks
capabilities.detail: Set callback_url on register or PATCH /me. Payloads are signed with HMAC-SHA256 in the X-Suwappu-Signature header. POST /webhooks/test sends a signed test event.

capabilities.title: Structured errors
capabilities.detail: Errors carry success, error, error_code, and sometimes details and hint. Codes include VALIDATION_ERROR, UNAUTHORIZED, WALLET_NOT_FOUND, QUOTE_NOT_FOUND, POLICY_VIOLATION and UPSTREAM_ERROR.

capabilities.title: OpenAPI and Postman
capabilities.detail: GET /v1/agent/openapi and GET /v1/agent/postman return the spec and a collection, so you can generate a client in any language.

Price a swap; returns quote_id and minimum_amount_out. 1 credit.
Dry run a quote. No signing, no broadcast. 1 credit.
Return an unsigned transaction, or 202 pending if approval is required.
Execute from a managed wallet. 5 credits. Accepts Idempotency-Key.
List webhook events; filter by status, event_type, limit, offset.
Send a signed test delivery to your callback_url.

specs.label: Free tier rate limit
specs.value: 30 requests per minute; HTTP 429 with Retry-After beyond it

specs.label: Executes funds
specs.value: Only /swap/execute (managed wallet). /swap returns an unsigned transaction.

example.title: Quote, then dry-run with the same wallet
example.code:
# 1. quote (wallet_address is required to build a real transaction)
curl -s -X POST https://api.suwappu.bot/v1/agent/quote \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SUWAPPU_API_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"from_token":"ETH","to_token":"USDC","amount":"0.1","chain":"base","wallet_address":"0xYourWallet"}'

# 2. dry run the returned quote_id with the same wallet
curl -s -X POST https://api.suwappu.bot/v1/agent/swap/simulate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SUWAPPU_API_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"quote_id":"QUOTE_ID","wallet_address":"0xYourWallet"}'

pages.pricing: Metered calls draw prepaid credits: a quote or dry run costs 1, a swap costs 5, and 1 credit is about $0.001. New agents get 100 starter credits (three grants per IP per day at most). Swap fees are 0.8% on EVM and 0.3% on Solana, 20% lower for World ID verified agents.
limits: A quote expires after 60 seconds. Request a fresh one if you wait.
Simulation is a dry run. It does not guarantee the swap will succeed at execution.
Quotes are not idempotent; only /swap/execute honours Idempotency-Key.
Webhook retry policy is not documented here, so treat webhooks as a convenience and reconcile with /swap/status.
Starter credits can be withheld by the per-IP guard.

faq.a: With /swap you sign with your own wallet; Suwappu never sees the key. With /swap/execute the managed wallet signs. Your suwappu_sk_ API key is shown once and only a hash is stored.

faq.q: What if a call fails or times out?
faq.a: Check GET /swap/status or /swaps first, then retry /swap/execute with the same Idempotency-Key. If the outcome is unknown, the charge is held and reconciled by that key.
Yes on /swap/execute, scoped to your agent and the request contents. A new key is a new trade. Quotes have no idempotency.

faq.q: Can I cap what an agent spends?
faq.a: Partly. A wallet spending limit caps the native-token value of each managed transaction; org-wide caps and approvals are set with the team. See spend-policies.
Approval and policy events are written to an audit log you can read at GET /v1/agent/audit. See approvals-audit.

whatItIs: There are two layers. Wallet policies belong to a managed wallet and are created with POST /v1/agent/wallet/policy. pages.metaDescription: Arbiter is a preview of escrow for agent work that pays on verified delivery. Demonstrated on NEAR testnet. Not enabled on the production API.
pages.headline: Escrow that pays on verified delivery.
pages.lead: Arbiter is a preview. It is shown on NEAR testnet only, with no mainnet funds, and its routes are not enabled on the production API yet.
whatItIs: Arbiter holds payment for agent work in escrow and releases it when delivery is verified against a rubric. The evidence is submitted as a blob, and the verdict is attested on NEAR testnet. The outputs on the Arbiter page are real testnet results, not mainnet activity.

It is a demo build, not a public API. The backend routes only mount when a server flag is on, and that flag is off by default. On 2026-11-21 these routes returned 404 on api.suwappu.bot. The header of the code says: no mainnet funds, no production payment paths.

pages.name: Agent Desk
pages.title: Agent Desk: give your agent a mandate, not your keys
pages.metaDescription: Agent Desk is a browser surface where an agent proposes swap sequences under a mandate and a human signs. WebMCP tools. Preview, not a public API.
pages.headline: Give your agent a mandate, not your keys.
pages.lead: Agent Desk is a preview. Agents in your browser propose swap sequences through WebMCP tools, and a human reviews, overrides and signs. It is not a public API.
whatItIs: Agent Desk is a page where a model operates a swap desk through WebMCP, the browser tool interface. You define a mandate, and the agent proposes sequences against it. A route dossier explains each route. The human stays at the signing step.

It exposes 16 static tools. Two more appear only at the right moment: request_override after a human blocks a step, and open_signing_handoff after a human approves. This is a demo surface. Its endpoints are not part of the public OpenAPI spec.

howItWorks.title: Set a mandate
howItWorks.detail: You state what the agent may do. The mandate bounds its proposals.

howItWorks.title: Agent proposes
howItWorks.detail: It calls tools such as propose-sequence to draft a swap sequence.

howItWorks.title: Review the route
howItWorks.detail: A route dossier shows how the swap would run.

howItWorks.title: Human decides
howItWorks.detail: You can block a step. The agent can then call request_override, which only exists after a block.

howItWorks.title: Sign yourself
howItWorks.detail: After approval, open_signing_handoff passes the transaction to you to sign.

more.title: Agent Swap Passport (preview)
more.body: Passport is a separate preview: an agent proves it is backed by a verified human through World ID, binds an ENS name, and requests swaps. It is not enabled on the production API; those routes returned 404 on api.suwappu.bot on 2026-11-21, and the server flag that mounts them is off by default. Only World ID is treated as a live signal in the demo; a second integration is shown as not integrated. In production, the World ID verified benefit that exists today is the 20% discount on the base swap fee (0.8% EVM, 0.3% Solana).
